_comment: Layout for 'Shabour_Winelist' -- a multi-page categorized price list (category > region/country/style > wine+price). UNIFIED (per explicit instruction 'make all pages like Vins au Verre'): every page now uses the SAME font/casing treatment via the document-wide defaults below, no per-page layout_overrides remain in the content file. category = SHABOUR SemiBold (dots/caps, default category_uppercase=true), subgroup = Avenir Next LT Pro Bold, kept in the case it was typed (default subgroup_uppercase=false), regardless of whether that category/subgroup pair happens to mean wine-style/country (Vins au Verre, Champagne et Effervescents) or country/sub-region (all other pages) -- the visual type scale is consistent even though the semantic meaning of each tier differs by page. This removes two earlier page-specific deviations: (1) the 'Champagne et Effervescents' page's subgroup=AvenirBook.ttf override from an earlier user-confirmed 'Bulles' fix, and (2) pages 3-11's category_uppercase='lower'. If either of those specific issues resurfaces, they were previously fixed via per-page layout_overrides and can be reapplied the same way. Page title also uses SHABOUR Semibold. SUPERSEDED SCALE NOTE: an earlier pass matched sizes against 'Winelist_FR_2026-08-11 (1).pdf' (margin_side 65->100, item_size 9->10, subgroup_size 11->9, gap_after_page_title 13->30). That PDF's own metadata (Producer/Creator) later turned out to be ReportLab -- i.e. it was a snapshot of THIS APP'S OWN earlier output, not a real InDesign export, so that whole matching pass was chasing our own prior state rather than the true original design. margin_side and gap_after_page_title are left as that pass set them (100 / 30) since no better evidence exists yet either way.  TRUE SCALE (read directly off the actual InDesign source, 'Shabour_Winelist_font settings.indd', via restaurant-provided screenshots of the Character panel per element -- the most authoritative source seen so far, since direct .indd/IDML parsing failed in this environment): page_title_size 18->25 (SHABOUR SemiBold), category_size 13->18 (SHABOUR SemiBold), item font Times-Roman->AvenirBook.ttf and item_size 10->9 (wine+price lines are Avenir Book, not serif), subgroup_size 9->8. These were only confirmed on the 'Vins au Verre' page (screenshots didn't cover the country/sub-region pages), but title/category/item are document-wide roles so applied globally; subgroup_size was extended globally as a type-scale assumption -- flagged, not independently verified for pages 3-11. IMPORTANT CORRECTION found in the same screenshots: on 'Vins au Verre'-style pages (category=wine style, subgroup=country), the font assignment was backwards in this file's per-page layout_overrides -- category should be SHABOUR-SemiBold.otf (dotted, e.g. 'CHAMPAGNE ET EFFERVESCENT'/'BLANC') and subgroup should be AvenirNextLTPro-Bold.ttf (e.g. 'France'/'Allemagne', title case, NOT lowercased) -- fixed on pages[1] ('Vins au Verre'). pages[2] ('Champagne et Effervescents') was NOT touched here: it still carries a deliberate subgroup=AvenirBook.ttf override from an earlier user-confirmed 'Bulles' fix that these screenshots don't address -- worth revisiting against the .indd file directly if the restaurant wants full consistency. Document-wide default subgroup font (AvenirBook.ttf, for pages 3-11's sub-region labels) was left untouched -- no screenshot evidence covers that role. At this new scale the document is still 13 pages ('Vins Rouges - France' overflows onto one automatic '(suite)' page, same as before). AVAILABLE SUBGROUP FONT OPTIONS (set per page via layout_overrides.fonts.subgroup, path relative to assets/fonts/): 'AvenirNextLTPro-Bold.ttf' (current default -- full alphabet, matches e.g. 'Galilee'), 'SHABOUR-SemiBold.otf' (full alphabet, rasterised, brand display face -- same font as category/page-title), 'ShoubourCut.otf' (a special cut of the brand face that ONLY has glyphs for N/Y, n/y and their accented forms -- every other letter is silently dropped, so real subgroup names will render mostly/entirely blank with it; only usable as-is for very short N/Y-heavy labels, not general region names, until a fuller version of that font file is provided). AVAILABLE CASING OPTIONS: layout_overrides.category_uppercase / subgroup_uppercase, each true (ALL CAPS) / 'lower' (all-lowercase) / false (keep as typed) -- category defaults true, subgroup defaults false. IMPORTANT, CORRECTED FINDING: SHABOUR-SemiBold.otf is NOT unicase -- capital letters and lowercase letters are genuinely different glyphs (confirmed via font table inspection: 'A' and 'a' map to different glyph names with different outlines/bounds) and render visibly differently: CAPITALS always carry the brand's decorative dot ('signs'), while lowercase letters render as a clean, dot-free form ('no signs'). This was mis-reported once earlier in this file as 'unicase / pixel-identical' based on a flawed low-resolution test; a corrected large-scale render (150pt) plus a live PDF render both confirm the dot only appears on capitals. Practical upshot: category_uppercase/subgroup_uppercase = true gives Shabour WITH signs, = 'lower' gives Shabour WITHOUT signs (same font file, no substitution needed) -- this is the mechanism to use for a 'with signs / without signs' toggle in Shabour itself, per-page via layout_overrides.
